title: 05 · Aerlo: boarding pass
strengths: Answers the queue question in one glance: KEF → CPH at 52 px, gate D7, boarding 07:05, seat 14A as the second hero, and the status pill 'On time · Gate closes 07:25' above the ticket.
Label-over-value grid with mono only for codes (AL 214, QX7-R4N), the Apple Wallet rhythm; 'Brightens at the gate' is a real product detail.
Believable itinerary: Wed 22 Oct, 07:40 to 12:55, 3h 15m nonstop, Mara Lindqvist, group 2, window.
slop_signals: A dot-matrix map with a route arc and a plane glyph fills a third of the ticket; it is texture, not information (the notes concede it is a diagram, not geography).
A stock-style 'wing above the clouds' photograph as the header: the airline cliché.
Punched notches and dashed perforations on a digital pass: skeuomorphism that Delta, Qantas and Apple Wallet no longer use.
fixes: Shrink the map to a thin route strip (Flighty's dotted line with a plane) or remove it and let the codes lead.
Replace the wing photo with a flat sky colour or the brand blue.
Keep one ticket-edge device: the perforation line or the notches, not both.

references.what: Huge airport codes, a strict label-over-value grid and a QR on a flat white pass with no map or notches.
QR first, seat and zone large, gate and boarding time as two tiles: the scan comes before the story.
Date, flight and seat in one row, airports with times below: a plainer grid that still reads in a queue.
The same map-texture-behind-codes device, here on a focus timer: shows how decorative it is.
A one-line dotted route with a plane glyph between codes: the route without a map.
